title: Security review (OWASP-style) of the lab apps

rows.finding: Admin route is guarded by requireAuth + requireRole('admin'); a normal user gets 403, a forged token gets 401.
JWT_SECRET fell back to a fixed lab secret if the variable was missing. Anyone who reads the code could forge tokens on a deployed copy.
rows.evidence: exp6_auth/server.js now stops in production when JWT_SECRET is missing

rows.finding: Passwords are stored with bcrypt (cost 10), never in plain text, and the hash is never sent to the browser.
Login accepted any JSON type for email and password, so {"$ne":null} objects could reach the query and bcrypt (an object password can also make bcrypt throw, which is a server error).
rows.evidence: login now accepts strings only; 2 tests

rows.finding: Search text is escaped before it becomes a regular expression, and sort fields come from a whitelist.
No front-end file uses innerHTML; text is inserted as text nodes only.
Login had no limit on attempts, so passwords could be guessed at full speed.
Request bodies are limited to 100 kb and page size to 50, so one request cannot flood memory.
Server sent 'X-Powered-By: Express' and no nosniff header.
The project had no .gitignore, so 'git add .' would have put the .env file (Gemini key) into GitHub.
Experiment 8 has no login on its student API. Acceptable for a lab demo, not for production. The capstone (Exp 15) puts the same data behind admin-only login.
Same message for unknown email and wrong password, tokens expire after 1 hour, expired tokens are rejected.
Unexpected errors are logged on the server and the browser only sees a generic message (no stack trace).
The Gemini key lives only in .env on the server. No browser file contains it or its variable name.
Dependencies are checked with npm audit (see the audit screenshot for the real result on the day).
